newsitem.title: UK: UK CBI sees interest rates rising.
newsitem.headline: UK CBI sees interest rates rising.

text.p: The Confederation of British Industry said Britain was set for robust economic growth over the next two years and official interest rates were likely to rise from the current 6.25 percent.
It sees interest rates rising to 6.5 percent in the third quarter of this year, 6.75 percent in the fourth quarter and then to 7.0 percent next year.

"This forecast assumes that sterling falls back from its present level. If it remains at its present high level, a further rise in interest rates will be less likely," it said in a press release on its latest economic forecasts.
The CBI said underlying retail price inflation (RPIX) was forecast to fall to 2.1 percent by the end of 1997, but was expected to rise throughout 1998, ending next year at 2.8 percent.
Output price inflation is expected to remain subdued through 1997, ending the year at 1.3 percent before rising to 2.2 percent by the end of 1998.
"This compares with our February forecast of 2.3 percent for the end of 1997 and 2.8 percent for the end of 1998," the CBI said.
The GDP forecast GDP growth at 3.1 percent in 1997 and 2.7 percent in 1998.
"The buoyant outlook largely reflects higher consumer spending growth due to higher real incomes and greater windfall gains than previously assumed," the CBI said.
"In contrast, weaker export growth than last year is still expected due to the strength of sterling."
CBI chief economic adviser Kate Barker said the forecasts assumed cautious fiscal policy to minimise upward pressure on interest rates.

Consumer spending was forecast to grow 4.4 percent this year and a further 3.5 percent in 1998. The savings ratio is expected to fall to 9.7 percent by the end of 1997 and rise to 10.7 percent by the end of 1998.
The public sector borrowing requirement (budget deficit) is expected to shrink to 15.6 billion stg in 1998/99, representing 1.9 percent of GDP, from 17.6 billion stg (2.2 percent of GDP) in 1997/98.
"The forecast assumes a fiscal tightening with an impact of three billion stg in 1997/98. The windfall tax is assumed to raise a net four billion stg in this financial year."
